writes.rule: Per subtopic seen: pMastery 0.7 if right at D2/D3, 0.55 if right at D1, 0.25 if wrong; level L0-L3 from the ladder step reached
Prerequisite-gap index = 100 x weighted misses / weighted items seen in slots 1-4, averaged over groups
Groups with the highest Part A percent (top 1-2, only if >= 65%)
Groups with the lowest Part A percent (bottom 1-2, only if < 65%)
Calibration = 1 - mean |confidence/5 - correct| over Part A (feeds the first MCI reading)
Highest difficulty answered correctly twice in a row: D1 low, D2 medium, D3 high
Verbal reasoning = percent of Part B verbal items right
Numerical reasoning = percent of Part B numerical items right
Abstract reasoning = percent of Part B abstract items right
Spatial reasoning = percent of Part B spatial items right
Logical deduction = percent right on Part B items tagged p65
Numeracy fluency = numerical percent scaled by speed (right answers under target time count 1.2x, max 100)
Processing speed = 100 x share of Part B items answered right within target seconds
RIASEC profile: each career-interest item scored 1-5; letter score = mean of its 2 items; top 3 letters form the code (e.g. IRC)

items.stem: Which of these numbers is a perfect square?
items.markingKey: C. 196. 14 x 14 = 196; the others are not the square of any whole number
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: multiplication facts and squares of numbers

items.stem: Which shows 36 written as a product of prime factors?
items.markingKey: A. 2 x 2 x 3 x 3. 4, 6 and 9 are not prime; 36 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 6-7: factors, primes and prime factorisation

items.stem: The prime factorisation of 180 is
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 6-7: factors, primes and prime factorisation

items.stem: 5⁴ means
items.markingKey: C. 5 x 5 x 5 x 5. The exponent 4 says how many 5s are multiplied
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: exponents and powers

items.stem: What is the value of 2⁵?
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: exponents and powers

items.stem: Which is greater, 3⁴ or 4³, and by how much?
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: exponents and powers

items.markingKey: C. -3. Start at -8 and move 5 to the right on the number line
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: integers and fractions, four operations

items.markingKey: C. 1/12. Common denominator 12: 9/12 - 8/12 = 1/12
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: integers and fractions, four operations

items.stem: A jug holds 2 1/2 litres of milk. 3/4 litre is used for tea and 1 1/3 litres for a pudding. How much milk is left?
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: integers and fractions, four operations

items.stem: Which digit can never be the units digit of a perfect square?
items.markingKey: D. 7. Squares end only in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9

items.stem: How many non-square numbers lie between 15² and 16²?
items.markingKey: A. 30. Between n² and (n+1)² there are 2n non-squares; 2 x 15 = 30

items.stem: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n². What is 1 + 3 + 5 + ... + 39?
items.markingKey: C. 400. 39 is the 20th odd number, so the sum is 20² = 400

items.subtopicHint: Square roots: prime factorisation and estimation

items.stem: Using prime factorisation, find √1764.
items.subtopicHint: Square roots: prime factorisation and estimation

items.stem: What is the smallest whole number by which 2352 must be multiplied to make it a perfect square?
items.subtopicHint: Square roots: prime factorisation and estimation
items.markingKey: C. 3. 2352 = 2⁴ x 3 x 7²; only the 3 is unpaired

items.stem: Which of these is a perfect cube?
What is the smallest number by which 1323 must be divided so that the quotient is a perfect cube?
items.markingKey: C. 49. 1323 = 3³ x 7²; dividing by 7² = 49 leaves 27 = 3³

items.stem: a³ x a⁴ = ?
items.subtopicHint: Exponent notation and laws of exponents
items.markingKey: B. a⁷. Same base: add the exponents, 3 + 4 = 7

items.subtopicHint: Exponent notation and laws of exponents

items.stem: If (5²)ˣ ÷ 5³ = 5⁵, what is x?
items.subtopicHint: Exponent notation and laws of exponents

items.stem: A potted plant is kept in a dark cupboard for 3 days. One leaf is then tested with iodine. What do you expect, and why?
items.answer: No blue-black colour, because no starch was made without light
options: No blue-black colour, because iodine reacts only with sugar
No blue-black colour, because no starch was made without light
Blue-black colour, because the plant made starch from soil water
Blue-black colour, because leaves always store starch
items.markingKey: B. No blue-black colour, because no starch was made without light. Iodine turns blue-black with starch; without light the plant uses up its starch and cannot make more
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: nutrition in plants (photosynthesis)

items.stem: In a circuit diagram, a long line drawn next to a short line stands for
items.markingKey: D. A cell. The long line is the positive terminal of a cell
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: electric circuits and their components

items.stem: A bulb does not glow when a rubber eraser closes the gap in a circuit, but glows with a steel key. This shows that
items.answer: steel is a conductor and rubber is an insulator
options: steel is a conductor and rubber is an insulator
both are conductors but rubber is weaker
rubber is a conductor and steel is an insulator
items.markingKey: A. steel is a conductor and rubber is an insulator. Current flows through conductors such as metals, not through insulators such as rubber
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: electric circuits and their components

items.stem: In an experiment, the factor you deliberately change is called the
items.markingKey: D. independent variable. You change the independent variable and measure the dependent one
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: planning a fair investigation

items.stem: A student wants to test whether salt makes ice melt faster. What must stay the same in both cups?
items.answer: The size of the ice cubes and the room temperature
options: Only the time she checks the result
The size of the ice cubes and the room temperature
items.markingKey: C. The size of the ice cubes and the room temperature. Only one factor (salt) should change; everything else is controlled
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: planning a fair investigation

items.stem: A student says plants grow taller with music. He plays music to one plant on a sunny window and keeps another plant, without music, in a dark corner. What is wrong with his test?
items.answer: Two factors (music and light) changed, so he cannot tell which caused the difference
options: He should have used three plants with music
Two factors (music and light) changed, so he cannot tell which caused the difference
Plants cannot hear, so no test is needed
He should measure the leaves, not the height
items.markingKey: B. Two factors (music and light) changed, so he cannot tell which caused the difference. A fair test changes one variable at a time
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: planning a fair investigation

items.stem: Digestion of starch begins in the
items.markingKey: C. mouth. Saliva contains an enzyme that starts breaking starch down
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: nutrition in animals (human digestive system)

items.stem: Why is the inner wall of the small intestine covered with finger-like villi?
items.answer: They increase the surface area for absorbing digested food
options: They increase the surface area for absorbing digested food
They push food back to the stomach
items.markingKey: A. They increase the surface area for absorbing digested food. More surface means faster absorption into the blood
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: nutrition in animals (human digestive system)

items.stem: A person whose gall bladder was removed is advised to eat less oily food. Which reason fits best?
items.answer: Bile, which breaks fat into small droplets, is no longer stored and released in large amounts
options: The stomach can no longer make acid
Fat is digested only in the gall bladder
Bile, which breaks fat into small droplets, is no longer stored and released in large amounts
items.markingKey: C. Bile, which breaks fat into small droplets, is no longer stored and released in large amounts. The gall bladder stores bile; without it less bile is available at mealtimes to emulsify fat
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: nutrition in animals (human digestive system)

items.stem: A testable 'if ... then ...' statement made before an experiment is called a
items.markingKey: D. hypothesis. A hypothesis is a prediction that an experiment can test

items.stem: Which of these is an observation, not an inference?
items.answer: The leaf has brown spots on it
options: The leaf has brown spots on it
The plant is sick because it got too much water
The spots were caused by a fungus
items.markingKey: A. The leaf has brown spots on it. An observation is what you can see or measure; the others are explanations or predictions

items.stem: Students found that seeds watered with tap water and with filtered water sprouted in the same number of days. Which conclusion is best supported?
items.answer: In this test, the type of water made no difference to sprouting time
options: Water is not needed for sprouting
In this test, the type of water made no difference to sprouting time
Filtered water is better for plants
items.markingKey: C. In this test, the type of water made no difference to sprouting time. A conclusion should not go beyond the data collected

items.stem: Curd is formed from milk by
items.markingKey: C. bacteria (Lactobacillus). Lactobacillus bacteria turn milk into curd

items.stem: Dough rises when yeast is added because
items.answer: yeast respires and releases carbon dioxide gas
options: yeast respires and releases carbon dioxide gas
items.markingKey: D. yeast respires and releases carbon dioxide gas. The carbon dioxide bubbles make the dough rise

items.stem: Why does food kept in a refrigerator spoil more slowly than food kept outside?
items.answer: Low temperature slows the growth of microorganisms
options: Microbes need light, which a fridge lacks
Low temperature slows the growth of microorganisms
items.markingKey: C. Low temperature slows the growth of microorganisms. Cold slows microbes; it does not kill all of them

items.stem: Which disease is caused by a virus?
items.markingKey: B. Chickenpox. Typhoid, tuberculosis and cholera are caused by bacteria

items.stem: How does a vaccine protect us?
items.answer: It trains the body to make antibodies so it can fight the real germ quickly later
options: It cures a disease after it starts
It trains the body to make antibodies so it can fight the real germ quickly later
It kills all germs in the body
items.markingKey: C. It trains the body to make antibodies so it can fight the real germ quickly later. Vaccines prepare the immune system in advance

items.stem: Malaria cases rise in a village after the monsoon. Which action targets the cause most directly?
items.answer: Remove stagnant water where mosquitoes breed
options: Remove stagnant water where mosquitoes breed
items.markingKey: D. Remove stagnant water where mosquitoes breed. Malaria spreads through mosquito bites; mosquitoes breed in stagnant water

items.stem: An electric iron works on the
items.subtopicHint: Heating and magnetic effects of current
items.markingKey: D. heating effect of current. Current through the heating coil produces heat

items.stem: Why is a fuse wire made of a material with a low melting point?
items.answer: It melts and breaks the circuit when too much current flows
items.subtopicHint: Heating and magnetic effects of current
options: It melts and breaks the circuit when too much current flows
It stops the wire getting magnetised
items.markingKey: B. It melts and breaks the circuit when too much current flows. The fuse melts first and protects the appliances

items.stem: A student winds insulated wire around an iron nail and connects it to a cell. The nail picks up 4 pins. How can she make it pick up more pins?
items.answer: Increase the number of turns of wire
items.subtopicHint: Heating and magnetic effects of current
options: Use a plastic rod instead of the nail
Increase the number of turns of wire
items.markingKey: C. Increase the number of turns of wire. More turns (or more current) make a stronger electromagnet

items.stem: Read: 'The old fort looked desolate; no one had visited it in years.' What does 'desolate' most likely mean?
items.markingKey: A. empty and lonely. 'No one had visited it in years' signals emptiness
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: working out word meaning from context

items.stem: Choose the correct word: Yesterday, Kabir ___ his bicycle to school.
items.markingKey: A. rode. 'Yesterday' needs the simple past
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: simple past and past continuous

items.stem: Choose the correct words: When the lights went out, we ___ dinner.
items.markingKey: A. were having. An action in progress in the past uses the past continuous
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: simple past and past continuous

items.stem: Choose the correct word: Each of the students ___ a library card.
items.markingKey: C. has. 'Each' is singular
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: subject-verb agreement

items.stem: Choose the correct word: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ aware of the change.
items.markingKey: C. were. With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'students'
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: subject-verb agreement

items.stem: Which sentence is correct?
items.answer: The bunch of keys was found under the sofa.
options: The bunch of keys was found under the sofa.
The bunch of keys were found under the sofa.
The bunch of keys are find under the sofa.
The bunch of keys have found under the sofa.
items.markingKey: A. The bunch of keys was found under the sofa.. The subject is 'bunch' (singular), not 'keys'
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: subject-verb agreement

items.stem: Read: "Bees visit flowers to collect nectar. As they move, pollen sticks to their bodies and is carried to other flowers. This helps plants make seeds." What is the passage mainly about?
items.answer: How bees help plants make seeds
options: How bees help plants make seeds
items.markingKey: A. How bees help plants make seeds. Every sentence builds towards pollination and seeds
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: reading for the main idea

items.stem: Read: "Arun practised the flute every evening, even when his friends called him out to play. At the school concert, the audience stood up and clapped for a long time." What is the main message?
options: Playing outside is a waste of time
items.markingKey: C. Steady practice leads to success. The practice in the first sentence explains the applause in the second
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: reading for the main idea

items.stem: Read: "Many cities now have car-free Sundays. Streets fill with cyclists, skaters and families. Shopkeepers first complained, but many now report more customers on foot." Which statement best sums up the passage?
items.answer: Car-free days, though doubted at first, benefit people and some businesses
options: Car-free days, though doubted at first, benefit people and some businesses
items.markingKey: C. Car-free days, though doubted at first, benefit people and some businesses. The summary must include both the early doubt and the later benefit
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: reading for the main idea

items.stem: Read: "The king gave his minister one coin and said, 'Fill this hall completely.' The minister bought a candle and lit it; its light filled every corner." What did the minister use to fill the hall?
items.subtopicHint: The Wit that Won Hearts: inference in a story
items.markingKey: C. Light from a candle. The last sentence says the light filled every corner

items.stem: Read: "The king gave his minister one coin and said, 'Fill this hall completely.' The minister bought a candle and lit it; its light filled every corner." What quality of the minister does this show?
items.subtopicHint: The Wit that Won Hearts: inference in a story
items.markingKey: B. Cleverness in solving a problem. He found an unexpected way to meet an impossible-sounding demand

items.stem: Read: "The king gave his minister one coin and said, 'Fill this hall completely.' The minister bought a candle and lit it; its light filled every corner." Why might the king have set this challenge?
items.answer: To test whether the minister could think beyond the obvious
items.subtopicHint: The Wit that Won Hearts: inference in a story
options: Because he wanted to save money
To test whether the minister could think beyond the obvious
items.markingKey: C. To test whether the minister could think beyond the obvious. Such challenges in stories test wit, not wealth

items.stem: 'To break the ice' means
items.answer: to start a conversation in an awkward situation
options: to start a conversation in an awkward situation
items.markingKey: B. to start a conversation in an awkward situation. An idiom has a meaning beyond its words

items.stem: Which word is closest in meaning to 'witty'?
items.markingKey: C. clever and amusing. A witty remark is quick, clever and funny

items.stem: Which sentence uses 'humble' correctly?
items.answer: Despite winning the prize, she stayed humble and thanked her team.
options: The road was humble with traffic.
Despite winning the prize, she stayed humble and thanked her team.
He humbled the cake in the oven.
The humble storm destroyed the bridge.
items.markingKey: B. Despite winning the prize, she stayed humble and thanked her team.. 'Humble' describes a modest person

items.stem: 'The moon is a silver coin' is an example of
items.subtopicHint: A Concrete Example: figures of speech in poetry
items.markingKey: C. a metaphor. It says the moon IS a coin, without 'like' or 'as'

items.stem: Which line contains personification?
items.answer: The wind whispered secrets to the trees.
items.subtopicHint: A Concrete Example: figures of speech in poetry
options: The wind whispered secrets to the trees.
The trees were as tall as towers.
items.markingKey: A. The wind whispered secrets to the trees.. Whispering secrets is a human action given to the wind

items.stem: In the line 'Hope is a lamp in a dark room', what does the poet suggest?
items.answer: Hope helps us see a way forward in difficult times
items.subtopicHint: A Concrete Example: figures of speech in poetry
options: Hope helps us see a way forward in difficult times
items.markingKey: D. Hope helps us see a way forward in difficult times. The dark room stands for hard times; the lamp lights the way

items.stem: Change to reported speech: Riya said, 'I am tired.'
items.answer: Riya said that she was tired.
items.subtopicHint: Wisdom Paves the Way: reported speech
options: Riya said that she was tired.
Riya told that I was tired.
Riya said that I am tired.
Riya said that she is being tired.
items.markingKey: A. Riya said that she was tired.. Change the pronoun and move the tense back

items.stem: Change to reported speech: The teacher said to us, 'Submit your projects tomorrow.'
items.answer: The teacher told us to submit our projects the next day.
items.subtopicHint: Wisdom Paves the Way: reported speech
options: The teacher told us to submit our projects the next day.
The teacher said submit your projects tomorrow.
The teacher asked that we submitted projects yesterday.
The teacher told us that submit projects tomorrow.
items.markingKey: A. The teacher told us to submit our projects the next day.. Commands become 'told ... to + verb'; 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'

items.stem: Change to reported speech: Aman asked me, 'Have you finished the book?'
items.answer: Aman asked me if I had finished the book.
items.subtopicHint: Wisdom Paves the Way: reported speech
options: Aman told me whether I finish the book.
Aman asked me if I had finished the book.
Aman asked me have I finished the book.
Aman asked me that had I finished the book.
items.markingKey: B. Aman asked me if I had finished the book.. Yes/no questions use 'if' or 'whether', normal word order and a backshifted tense

items.stem: India lies entirely in which two hemispheres?
items.markingKey: B. Northern and Eastern. India lies north of the Equator and east of the Prime Meridian
items.prerequisiteNote: Class 7: maps, latitudes and longitudes

items.stem: Who founded the Mughal Empire in India in 1526?
items.subtopicHint: Delhi Sultanate and the coming of the Mughals
items.markingKey: A. Babur. Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526
items.prerequisiteNote: Class 7: Delhi Sultanate and Mughal Empire

items.stem: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between
items.subtopicHint: Delhi Sultanate and the coming of the Mughals
items.markingKey: C. Babur and Ibrahim Lodi. Akbar fought Hemu at the Second Battle of Panipat (1556)
items.prerequisiteNote: Class 7: Delhi Sultanate and Mughal Empire

items.stem: In a democracy, the government is chosen by
items.markingKey: D. the people through elections. Democracy means rule by the people
items.prerequisiteNote: Class 7: democracy and government

items.stem: Which is an example of universal adult franchise?
items.answer: Every citizen aged 18 or above can vote, whatever their income or gender
options: Every citizen aged 18 or above can vote, whatever their income or gender
items.markingKey: B. Every citizen aged 18 or above can vote, whatever their income or gender. 'Universal' means no citizen adult is left out
items.prerequisiteNote: Class 7: democracy and government

items.stem: Why does India hold general elections every five years instead of electing a government for life?
items.answer: So people can judge the government's work and change it if they wish
options: So people can judge the government's work and change it if they wish
Because the Constitution was written in five years
Because leaders must retire after five years
items.markingKey: A. So people can judge the government's work and change it if they wish. Regular elections keep the government accountable to the people
items.prerequisiteNote: Class 7: democracy and government

items.stem: Which of these is a renewable resource?
items.markingKey: D. Solar energy. Sunlight is replenished naturally; fossil fuels are not
items.prerequisiteNote: Class 7: our environment and resources

items.stem: Black soil is best suited for growing
items.markingKey: D. cotton. Black (regur) soil holds moisture and suits cotton
items.prerequisiteNote: Class 7: our environment and resources

items.stem: A village depends on one well whose water level drops every summer. Which step uses the resource most sustainably?
items.answer: Harvest rainwater to recharge the groundwater
options: Dig the well deeper every year
Harvest rainwater to recharge the groundwater
Pump more water in winter to store
items.markingKey: C. Harvest rainwater to recharge the groundwater. Recharging puts water back; the others only take more out
items.prerequisiteNote: Class 7: our environment and resources

items.stem: Resources that are replenished naturally and can be used again and again are called
items.markingKey: D. renewable resources. Renewable resources renew themselves over a short time

items.stem: Which pair shows a natural resource and something made from it?
items.answer: Iron ore and a steel bridge
options: Iron ore and a steel bridge
A steel bridge and iron ore
items.markingKey: A. Iron ore and a steel bridge. Iron ore is natural; steel is made from it

items.stem: Why is conserving fossil fuels important for the future?
items.answer: They take millions of years to form, so they can run out
options: They take millions of years to form, so they can run out
They are found only in India
items.markingKey: B. They take millions of years to form, so they can run out. Fossil fuels are non-renewable on a human time scale

items.stem: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal?
items.markingKey: D. Shah Jahan. Shah Jahan built it in Agra in memory of Mumtaz Mahal

items.stem: Which Mughal emperor is known for the policy of sulh-i-kul, or peace with all?
items.markingKey: D. Akbar. Akbar promoted tolerance among different faiths

items.stem: Why did many regional kingdoms grow powerful in the 18th century?
items.answer: The Mughal Empire weakened after Aurangzeb, so governors and local rulers became independent
options: The Mughal Empire weakened after Aurangzeb, so governors and local rulers became independent
The Delhi Sultanate had just been founded
The British handed power to them
items.markingKey: A. The Mughal Empire weakened after Aurangzeb, so governors and local rulers became independent. A weaker centre allowed regional powers to rise

items.stem: The council of eight ministers that helped Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj govern was called the
items.subtopicHint: Maratha administration: Ashta Pradhan, forts and navy
items.markingKey: A. Ashta Pradhan. Ashta Pradhan means council of eight ministers

items.stem: The Marathas built a navy and many forts along the western coast mainly to
items.answer: defend the coast and control sea trade
items.subtopicHint: Maratha administration: Ashta Pradhan, forts and navy
options: defend the coast and control sea trade
items.markingKey: D. defend the coast and control sea trade. Sea forts such as Sindhudurg guarded the Konkan coast

items.stem: The Peshwas of the Maratha state were originally
items.answer: chief ministers who later became the real power in the state
items.subtopicHint: Maratha administration: Ashta Pradhan, forts and navy
options: chief ministers who later became the real power in the state
items.markingKey: A. chief ministers who later became the real power in the state. Peshwa means chief minister; by the 18th century they led the state

items.stem: In which year did the English East India Company win the Battle of Plassey?
items.subtopicHint: Expansion of East India Company rule
items.markingKey: B. 1757. Plassey (1757) gave the Company control of Bengal

items.stem: Under the 'Doctrine of Lapse', a kingdom
items.answer: was taken over by the Company if the ruler died without a natural heir
items.subtopicHint: Expansion of East India Company rule
options: was taken over by the Company if the ruler died without a natural heir
items.markingKey: C. was taken over by the Company if the ruler died without a natural heir. Lord Dalhousie used it to annex Satara and Jhansi

items.stem: Under the subsidiary alliance, an Indian ruler who accepted it had to
items.answer: keep British troops in his state and pay for them
items.subtopicHint: Expansion of East India Company rule
options: keep British troops in his state and pay for them
items.markingKey: D. keep British troops in his state and pay for them. Lord Wellesley used it to bring states under Company control without war

items.stem: What number comes next? 3, 7, 11, 15, ?
If 4 identical notebooks cost 96, what do 7 notebooks cost at the same rate?
25% of 80 is the same as 50% of which number?
What number comes next? 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
Book is to reading as fork is to ...
items.explanation: A book is used for reading; a fork is used for eating

items.stem: Which word does not belong with the others? apple, mango, carrot, banana
items.explanation: Carrot is a vegetable; the others are fruits

items.stem: All squares are rectangles. All rectangles have four sides. Which statement must be true?
options: Some rectangles do not have four sides
items.explanation: If every square is a rectangle and every rectangle has four sides, every square has four sides

items.stem: Asha is taller than Ben. Ben is taller than Chitra. Dev is shorter than Chitra. Who is the shortest?
The shapes repeat in a pattern: circle, square, triangle, circle, square, ? Which shape comes next?
items.explanation: The three shapes repeat in the same order

items.stem: Figure 1 has 1 black dot, figure 2 has 2 white dots, figure 3 has 3 black dots, figure 4 has 4 white dots. What is figure 5?
items.explanation: One more dot each time; colours alternate

items.stem: Which letter comes next? A, C, F, J, O, ?
items.explanation: The gaps grow by one: +2, +3, +4, +5, then +6

items.stem: Rule: the third figure keeps the lines that appear in only one of the first two figures and drops lines they share. A vertical line '|' and a horizontal line '-' give a cross '+'. If figure 1 is a cross '+' and figure 2 is a vertical line '|', what is figure 3?
items.explanation: The vertical line is shared, so it is dropped; the horizontal line stays

items.stem: A square sheet of paper is folded in half once along a diagonal. What shape do you get?
items.explanation: The diagonal fold puts one corner on the opposite corner

items.stem: A mirror is held upright beside each capital letter. Which letter looks the same in the mirror?
items.explanation: A has a vertical line of symmetry

items.stem: A cube is painted on all faces and cut into 27 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly two painted faces?
items.explanation: Those are the middle cubes of the 12 edges

items.stem: You face north. You turn 90° clockwise, then 180°, then 90° anticlockwise. Which way do you face now?

items.prompt: On a normal school day, how long do you study at home (not counting tuition)?
When do you usually study best?
How long is a typical study session before you take a break?
How often do you revise topics you have already finished?
How do you usually revise?

options.label: Testing myself with flashcards or quizzes

items.prompt: I put off starting homework until the last minute.
Where is your phone while you study?

options.label: With me, I check it often

Do you prefer studying alone or with others?
When you get stuck on a question, what do you usually do first?

options.label: Search online or watch a video

options.label: Yes, for two or more subjects

I like hard problems, even when I might get them wrong.
Before a test, how nervous do you usually feel?
